## Exact counterexample to the printed k107 product

Refutes the literal invariant in both arXiv v11 Table 2 and the published journal Table 2. In the ellipse with axes 4 and 3, two primitive convex four-period billiard orbits share the confocal caustic with axes 16/5 and 9/5, but give k107 values 288/625 and 625/1152.

The proof checks the source's original-orbit half angles and outer tangent polygon, provides a continuous T²=−id family connecting the examples, and verifies common caustic, physical reflection and all nonzero denominators. Signed and ordinary areas coincide because both examples are convex and counterclockwise.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. The frozen proof is unchanged. All 10,073 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically; 8,397 independent rational/symbolic controls pass. Eight review files are included.

Two substantive approach families are recorded (2/5). This resolves the printed assertion by counterexample. It does not claim a corrected quotient/parity theorem, historical priority, or human peer review. The related k108 and earlier k603/k405 targets are distinct. The coordinating task owns the claimed_solved queue update.
